title: Native Execution Engine and JVM Spark: how they divide one query
purpose: Native and JVM execution compared. Shared responsibilities; What only the JVM path does; What the native path changes; Cost of mixing; How they work together in one plan.
accessibleSummary: Native and JVM execution compared. Shared responsibilities; What only the JVM path does; What the native path changes; Cost of mixing; How they work together in one plan.
longDescription: Native and JVM execution compared. Shared responsibilities; What only the JVM path does; What the native path changes; Cost of mixing; How they work together in one plan.

nodes.label: Planning, scheduling and memory
nodes.summary: Planning, scheduling, shuffle and memory management are identical on both paths.
nodes.detail: Planning, scheduling, shuffle and memory management are identical on both paths.
nodes.whyItMatters: Planning, scheduling, shuffle and memory management are identical on both paths.

evidence.note: NEE preserves existing query optimizer behaviours including adaptive query execution and predicate pushdown.

processing: Optimize, schedule and manage memory identically
outputs: One physical plan and one task graph
drill.example: AQE coalesces post-shuffle partitions the same way whether or not the engine is enabled.
failureModes: Assuming native execution removes the need to tune partitions or fix skew.

nodes.label: Storage and correctness contracts
nodes.summary: Both paths read and write the same OneLake Delta tables with the same semantics.
nodes.detail: Both paths read and write the same OneLake Delta tables with the same semantics.
nodes.whyItMatters: Both paths read and write the same OneLake Delta tables with the same semantics.

evidence.note: The native execution engine supports Parquet and Delta formats across the Spark APIs.

processing: Read and write through the same Delta protocol
drill.example: A table written with the engine on is indistinguishable to any other Fabric engine.
failureModes: Expecting a storage-level change; the difference is execution only.

nodes.label: JVM / Tungsten path
nodes.summary: The JVM path executes row-at-a-time with whole-stage codegen and covers every operator.
nodes.detail: The JVM path executes row-at-a-time with whole-stage codegen and covers every operator.
nodes.whyItMatters: The JVM path executes row-at-a-time with whole-stage codegen and covers every operator.

evidence.note: CODEGEN mode prints the generated code, confirming whole-stage fusion on the JVM path.

drill.example: A filter and projection compile into a single loop marked with a *(1) prefix.
failureModes: A Python UDF breaks fusion and returns the stage to interpreted evaluation.

nodes.label: Native / Velox path
nodes.summary: The native path executes columnar batches with vectorized C++ but covers only supported operators.
nodes.detail: The native path executes columnar batches with vectorized C++ but covers only supported operators.
nodes.whyItMatters: The native path executes columnar batches with vectorized C++ but covers only supported operators.

evidence.note: Velox performs vectorized SIMD columnar execution of the Substrait plan Gluten produces.
Supported operators are offloaded to a vectorized C++ path providing columnar SIMD-accelerated processing.

drill.example: An aggregation over one column runs as a vectorized pass rather than per-row evaluation.
failureModes: Coverage is partial and changes per release, so support cannot be assumed.

nodes.label: Known correctness divergences
nodes.summary: A small set of documented behaviours differ between Velox and vanilla Spark.
nodes.detail: A small set of documented behaviours differ between Velox and vanilla Spark.
nodes.whyItMatters: A small set of documented behaviours differ between Velox and vanilla Spark.

evidence.note: NEE casting from DECIMAL to FLOAT diverges from vanilla Spark, which round-trips through a string conversion.
round() can return different results because Velox uses the C++ standard library implementation.
collect_list and collect_set use ARRAY as the intermediate aggregation type under NEE rather than BINARY.

outputs: Results that may differ from vanilla Spark in specific cases
drill.example: A DECIMAL-to-FLOAT cast can produce a different value than the same query on the JVM path.
controls: Regression-test critical numeric and ordering logic across both paths
failureModes: Silent numeric drift in financial calculations if parity is assumed rather than tested.

nodes.label: One plan, per-operator routing
nodes.summary: A single query routinely runs partly native and partly JVM, paying a conversion at each boundary.
nodes.detail: A single query routinely runs partly native and partly JVM, paying a conversion at each boundary.
nodes.whyItMatters: A single query routinely runs partly native and partly JVM, paying a conversion at each boundary.

evidence.note: A plan that falls back mid-flight can be slower than running with NEE off entirely, because conversion overhead is paid without sustained native execution.

inputs: A plan with both supported and unsupported operators
processing: Route each operator to its path
drill.example: Repeated VeloxColumnarToRowExec nodes reveal a plan alternating between paths.
controls: Restructure the query to group native work together
failureModes: Many small native islands cost more in conversion than the vectorization saves.

nodes.label: Choosing deliberately
nodes.summary: Native execution suits compute-bound work; ANSI mode forces a per-workload decision on Runtime 2.0.
nodes.detail: Native execution suits compute-bound work; ANSI mode forces a per-workload decision on Runtime 2.0.
nodes.whyItMatters: Native execution suits compute-bound work; ANSI mode forces a per-workload decision on Runtime 2.0.

evidence.note: The ANSI-versus-native trade-off on Runtime 2.0 is a per-workload decision recorded in the Environment.
Native execution is toggled per application with spark.native.enabled.

processing: Decide native versus ANSI per workload class
drill.example: A data-quality-critical silver pipeline keeps ANSI on; a scan-heavy gold aggregation prefers native speed.
failureModes: A global decision applied to every workload gets one of the two classes wrong.
